features.quote: the model declares completion, - the model gives up, - a max-turn limit is reached
Define explicit stop conditions: - model requests to stop - repeated identical failure after N cycles - max token or turn cap - environment crash
Use these carefully because some failure classes are “more fair” than others.
features.justification_quote: That may be desirable if you want stress response, but it confounds interpretation.

features.quote: Avoid “impossible” tasks that are obviously impossible from the start
features.justification_quote: because then the model may simply refuse or give up immediately.

features.quote: A model saying “this may be impossible” after evidence accumulates is not necessarily unstable.
features.justification_quote: This is one of the most important confounds.
A model that explicitly notes failure may score high on self-criticism even if it is behaving rationally.
A task that is merely hard may inflate instability for weaker models, which is a different phenomenon.

features.quote: Overly adversarial setup may induce generic refusal
features.justification_quote: If the model detects the trap too early, it may just refuse or hedge.
Without baseline, you may confuse “bad at coding” with “rattled under failure.”

features.quote: repeated adversarial failure may be undesirable for other reasons
